subject: Multi-region transfer playbook + MSA/Order Form tie-outs
messages:
From: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-09-21T08:45:00Z
Subject: Draft playbook for CuraHealth (transfer impact + MSAs)

Team — looping you in on a cross-functional sync for CuraHealth (RWI-4521). They returned new redlines to the DPA and added an SCCs exhibit that references an EU->US transfer carveout. Key asks from legal: 1) confirm processor/processor role mapping in the Order Form exhibits, 2) propose mitigation language for the transfer-impact addendum, 3) provide evidence we can supply for their privacy team (KMS boundary, subprocessor roster snapshot, audit logs sample).

I attached a consolidated redline (CuraHealth_DPA_v3_redline.docx) and an evidence matrix to populate. For initial run: Laura — can you validate the proposed delegation language and flag anything we can’t accept? Ben — pricing/product callouts that hinge on routing (multi-region) — quick note please. Jonas — any runtime/service constraints for retained logs or export controls? Stephanie — I’ll need a short summary for the AE to send with the legal package.

Goal: a coordinated external response and an optional short playbook for the customer that lists fallback routing options and evidentiary artifacts. I suggest a 30-min legal+product check on Thursday. Thoughts?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Enterprise Sales Ops
Redwood Inference
From: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
To: Marina Alvarez <marina.alvarez@curahealth.com>, contracts@curahealth.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-09-22T14:12:00Z
Subject: Re: CuraHealth DPA redlines — proposed next steps

Marina / team — thanks for the redlines and the SCCs exhibit. We reviewed at a high level and pulled together an internal checklist. Attached is our consolidated redline (CuraHealth_DPA_v3_redline.docx) that includes inline comments where we need clarification. High-level items we want to call out up front: 

- Processor roles: we propose to mirror the Order Form Exhibit B processor mapping; any additional role delegation requests will need a subprocessor addendum.
- Transfer impact: we can offer a Transfer Addendum that references the SCCs exhibit, proposes contractual fallback to EU-hosted processing for specified PII datasets, and a temporary cross-border routing exception window for a maximum of 90 days while we enable region routing.
- Evidence: we can deliver a subprocessor roster snapshot, an anonymized audit log sample, and KMS proof-of-separation (HSM provider cert).

If that approach sounds acceptable we’ll schedule a short walkthrough and attach the evidence matrix. Can you confirm for which data classes CuraHealth expects EU-only residency and the timeline they're targeting for the change?

Best,
Vanessa

Attachment: CuraHealth_DPA_v3_redline.docx (track changes + comment summary)
From: Marina Alvarez <marina.alvarez@curahealth.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com, contracts@curahealth.com
Date: 2027-09-23T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: CuraHealth DPA redlines — proposed next steps

Thanks Vanessa — that is helpful. Quick clarifications from our side:

- Data classes: PHI-derived telemetry and patient consent recordings must be EU-resident within 6 months; we can accept a 90-day temporary routing exception to stand up EU routing.
- SCCs language: our counsel wants the SCCs exhibit to include specific subprocessors (we provided a draft list) and a clause that requires 30 days notice for any new subprocessor.
- Evidence: the roster and audit sample look sufficient for now; we will follow up on KMS provider cert.

We are fine with a short joint session. Can you include product engineering on the call so we can discuss timeline implications for EU-hosted routing? Proposed times: Thursday 10:00-10:30 or Friday 16:00 (CEST).

Regards,
Marina Alvarez
Legal Counsel, CuraHealth

On Thu, Sep 23, 2027 at 08:15 Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Marina — adding internal owners. We can do Thursday 10:00 CEST. I’ll send calendar invite with required artifacts.
From: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-09-24T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft playbook for CuraHealth (transfer impact + MSAs)

Vanessa — quick legal read-through notes after looking at CuraHealth's requested edits: 

1) Subprocessor notice period: we can accept 30 days for new subprocessors but propose a carveout for emergency replacements (72 hours with post-facto notice) — provided the replacement is bound by the same contractual safeguards.
2) SCCs exhibit: redline includes our preferred insertion that clarifies that the SCCs apply to the extent permitted by applicable law and the parties will cooperate on any lawful blocking statute claim.
3) Transfer Addendum: we will offer (A) temporary routing exception (90 days) + (B) timeline commitment to prioritize EU-hosted routing work in our roadmap (we should attach a product commitment summary but label it non-binding schedule).

I flagged a couple of technical evidence asks that look like operational requests (audit log retention beyond our default — product will need to confirm). If Jonas confirms we can deliver the sample without extended retention, we’ll be set.

I’ll prepare a short summary doc we can share on the call.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-09-27T16:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft playbook for CuraHealth (transfer impact + MSAs)

Short product ops update for the record: 

- EU-hosted routing: engineering confirms we can enable region-based routing per customer for the main inference path within ~8 weeks if prioritized; initial rollout will cover generation APIs and embeddings but not legacy batch export paths.
- Audit logs: we can provide an anonymized sample from existing retention without changing default retention windows. Extended retention is possible via a feature request; that will be a separate product delivery and not part of this contract.
- Subprocessor emergency replacements: operations can implement a 72-hour emergency replacement process with a post-deployment attestation to the customer.

Next steps: Laura to finalize redline with the emergency replacement clause, Vanessa to confirm the call time with CuraHealth and attach the summary + evidence matrix.

Jonas Weber
Sr. Product Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
